_readme: Per-animal, per-jurisdiction legal status, for the legal hub and its US map.
STATUS VALUES, which are the map's colour buckets:
banned      cannot be kept as a pet, no permit route exists
permit      legal, but a permit or licence is required first
conditional legal without a permit only if a stated condition is met
legal       expressly allowed by name in the jurisdiction's own rules
(absent)    no state-level rule found. The map leaves these uncoloured.
'absent' is deliberately not a value. A missing entry means not yet
researched OR researched and found to have no rule, and those must not be
conflated: see coverage.researched below for which jurisdictions have
actually been read. Only claim 'no restriction' for a jurisdiction listed
Every entry carries a sourceId into `sources` plus the citation and, where
short enough, the operative wording. Primary sources only: the regulation,
statute or the enforcing agency's own page. Never a secondary summary.
NYC is a separate jurisdiction from NY because its Health Code is stricter
than state law and covers 8 million people. Same principle would apply to
any other city rule worth mapping.

coverage.note: Statuses are complete for the 19 jurisdictions in coverage.researched. An animal with no entry for one of those has no rule there. An animal with no entry for any other jurisdiction simply has not been researched yet, and must not be shown as unrestricted.

ca-671.title: California Code of Regulations Title 14 § 671, via CDFW Restricted Species Laws and Regulations Manual
ca-671.note: § 671(b) defines (D) detrimental and (W) welfare. § 671.1(a) lists permit types; none covers pet keeping. The only possession permit, Animal Care, requires lawful possession in California before January 1992.

ga-391-4-8-05.title: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 391-4-8-.05, Wild Animals, License Required

ga-dnr-exotics.title: Georgia DNR Law Enforcement, Wild Animals/Exotics
ga-dnr-exotics.note: States the enforcement position: 'The exotic species listed below, except where otherwise noted, may not be held as pets in Georgia.'

hi-4-71-6.title: Hawaii Administrative Rules § 4-71-6, List of Prohibited Animals
hi-4-71-6.note: Also carries the default rule: introduction is 'prohibited except for those animals on the lists' incorporated in § 4-71-6.5.

hi-4-71-6-5.title: Hawaii Administrative Rules § 4-71-6.5, List of Restricted Animals, Part A (research and exhibition)

pa-2961.title: 34 Pa.C.S. § 2961, definition of exotic wildlife
pa-2961.note: Names only bears, coyotes, lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars, cheetahs, cougars, wolves and crossbreeds. The hedgehog and sugar glider bans rest on 'includes, but is not limited to'.

pa-memo-44994.title: Pennsylvania House co-sponsorship memo 44994, Rep. David Zimmerman, 14 January 2025
pa-memo-44994.note: Confirms the mechanism: hedgehogs and sugar gliders 'are banned from ownership as pets through the Game Commission's regulations and their interpretation of Title 34.'

dc-8-1808.title: D.C. Code § 8-1808(j), Prohibited conduct
dc-8-1808.note: Closed list. Seven permitted categories; everything else is barred as a household pet.

nyc-161-01.title: NYC Health Code Article 161.01(b), list of animals illegal to keep as pets

nj-7-25-4-4.title: N.J.A.C. 7:25-4.4 Exempted Species and 7:25-4.5 Additional Species
nj-7-25-4-4.note: 4.4 is a closed exempt list; 4.5 requires a permit for 'any other' exotic species not exempted.

me-unrestricted.title: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, Unrestricted Species List
me-unrestricted.note: Species needing no importation, exhibition or possession permit.

wi-169.title: Wisconsin Statutes Chapter 169, Captive Wildlife
wi-169.note: § 169.01(37) defines wild animal; § 169.11(1)(a) designates harmful wild animals as cougars, ursidae, wild and feral swine. § 169.04(4)(b) exempts most non-native species from licensing.

fl-prohibited.title: Florida FWC Prohibited Nonnative Species List (Ch. 68-5, F.A.C.)
fl-prohibited.note: 16 high-risk reptiles added 25 Feb 2021, effective 29 April 2021. Prohibited species may be possessed only by permit for educational exhibition, research or eradication. Tegu and green iguana owners who held one before 29 April 2021 and applied by October 2021 keep a no-cost, non-transferable personal permit for that animal's life.

ny-11-0103.title: N.Y. Environmental Conservation Law § 11-0103(6)(e), definition of wild animal
ny-11-0103.note: A closed definition: 'includes and is limited to' nonhuman primates and prosimians, Felidae and hybrids, Canidae, Ursidae, venomous reptiles plus named large pythons and monitors, and Crocodylia. § 11-0512 then bars possessing a wild animal as a pet, grandfathering animals held when the section took effect if licensed within six months.

ct-26-40a.title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 26-40a, Possession of potentially dangerous animal
ct-26-40a.note: Potentially dangerous animals are 'the felidae... the canidae... the ursidae... and the hominidae', or any hybrid. Narrow: no rodents, marsupials, mustelids or insectivores. Civil penalty up to $2,000 per offence and a class A misdemeanour for a wilful violation.

ma-321-9-01.title: 321 CMR 9.01, Exemption List
ma-321-9-01.note: A closed exemption list of wild vertebrates that may be imported, sold or possessed without a permit. Anything not exempt needs one. Criteria include no significant ecological risk if released and care no more demanding than a common domesticated pet.

ma-131-77.title: M.G.L. c. 131 § 77, and 321 CMR 9.02 List of Domestic Animals
ma-131-77.note: Ferrets are handled as domestic animals under 9.02 rather than on the 9.01 exemption list.

co-w11.title: Colorado 2 CCR 406-11, Chapter W-11, Wildlife Parks and Unregulated Wildlife, § 1103(B)
co-w11.note: 'No license is required for the private possession or purchase of animals, which are included on the unregulated wildlife list or the domestic animal list.' Unregulated does not mean unmonitored: importation rules and local ordinances still apply.

az-r12-4-406.title: Ariz. Admin. Code R12-4-406, Restricted Live Wildlife
az-r12-4-406.note: Restricted wildlife requires the applicable federal licences and permits, an appropriate special licence, or a lawful exemption.

or-609-305.title: Or. Rev. Stat. § 609.305, 'Exotic animal' defined, with § 609.341 permit requirement
or-609-305.note: A closed definition: non-indigenous Felidae except the domestic cat, nonhuman primates, non-wolf non-indigenous Canidae except the domestic dog, bears other than the black bear, and Crocodylia. § 609.341 bars keeping one without an ODA permit, and permits had to pre-date the 2009 Act, so the practical answer for a listed animal is no. Cities and counties may prohibit exotic animals by ordinance on top of this.

wa-rcw-16-30.title: Wash. Rev. Code ch. 16.30, Dangerous Wild Animals, § 16.30.010(2) and § 16.30.030
wa-rcw-16-30.note: An enumerated definition. Felidae is limited to lions, tigers, captive-bred cougars, jaguars, cheetahs, leopards, snow leopards and clouded leopards; Canidae to wolves excluding wolf-hybrids. § 16.30.030: 'A person shall not own, possess, keep, harbor, bring into the state, or have custody or control of a potentially dangerous wild animal', grandfathering lawful possession before 22 July 2007.

oh-935-01.title: Ohio Rev. Code § 935.01, Dangerous Wild Animals and Restricted Snakes definitions
oh-935-01.note: Two enumerated lists. Dangerous wild animals need an Ohio Department of Agriculture wildlife shelter permit; anything on neither list needs no state permit. Restricted snakes are constrictors of 12 feet or more plus venomous families.

tx-822-101.title: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 822.101(4) and § 822.103, Dangerous Wild Animals
tx-822-101.note: A closed species list. § 822.103: 'a person may not own, harbor, or have custody or control of a dangerous wild animal for any purpose unless the person holds a certificate of registration for that animal issued by an animal registration agency', plus liability insurance of at least $100,000 per occurrence and caging standards.

CA.quote: Order Insectivora-Shrews, Moles, Hedgehogs, etc. All species (D)

GA.note: Rule says licence required; DNR states listed species may not be held as pets, and hedgehogs have no carve-out.

HI.quote: The introduction into Hawaii of live animals or live non-domestic animals ... is prohibited except for those animals on the lists
HI.note: Not named. Barred by the default rule. The only hedgehog Hawaii names is Hemiechinus auritis, not the pet species.

PA.note: No statute names hedgehogs. Game Commission interpretation. Legislation to reverse it has been introduced every session since 2017.

DC.note: Closed list permits 'domesticated rodents and rabbits'. Hedgehogs are Eulipotyphla, not rodents, so no category fits.

NYC.quote: Insectivorous mammals (Insectivora): All aardvark, anteater, shrew, otter shrew, gymnure, desman, tenrec, mole and hedgehog.

NJ.note: Absent from the 4.4 exempt list, so 4.5 requires a permit.

ME.quote: Atelerix albiventris  Four-toed Hedgehog, African Pygmy Hedgehog
ME.note: Commonly misreported as a permit state.

WI.note: Not a designated harmful wild animal; Ch. 169 licensing does not reach it. Commonly misreported as a permit state.

FL.note: No mammal entry covers hedgehogs; the 2021 rule is reptile-focused.

NY.note: Not within the closed definition of wild animal. Legal statewide, but banned in New York City under its own Health Code.

MA.note: Named on the exemption list. The regulation uses the older genus Erinaceus; current nomenclature is Atelerix albiventris.

CO.quote: African pygmy hedgehog (Atelerix albiventris, Erinaceus albiventris)
CO.note: On the unregulated wildlife list, so no state licence.

AZ.quote: All species of the order Erinaceomorpha. Common names include: European hedgehogs, gymnures, and moonrats. Except members of the genus Atelerix, which are not restricted.
AZ.note: Arizona restricts hedgehogs as an order and then exempts the pet genus by name, so the African pygmy is legal and the European is not.

OR.note: Outside the statutory definition of exotic animal.

OH.note: On neither list, so no state permit.

TX.note: Not on the list. Texas requires no state permit for an animal that is not listed, not endangered and not native wildlife.

GA.quote: European ferret (Mustela putorius furo) may be sold, purchased, exhibited, or held as a pet without a license or permit
GA.note: Condition: neutered before seven months and vaccinated against rabies.

NYC.quote: All fur bearing mammals of the family Mustelidae, including ... stoat and ferret.

NY.note: Mustelidae is absent from the definition. NYC bans it separately.

MA.note: Treated as a domestic animal under 321 CMR 9.02, but M.G.L. c. 131 § 77 requires it to be surgically neutered or spayed and incapable of breeding.

CO.quote: Domesticated races of European ferret (Mustela putorius)

AZ.note: No Mustelidae entry in the restricted mammal list.

OR.note: Mustelidae is not in the definition.

TX.note: Legal statewide, though some cities restrict ferrets by ordinance.

CA.quote: Order Marsupialia-Marsupials or Pouched Animals: All species (W)

GA.quote: Petaurus breviceps (sugar glider) may be sold, purchased, exhibited, or held as a pet without a license or permit if the owner thereof possesses valid documentation that the animal originated from a source inspected and regulated by the United States Department of Agriculture

PA.note: Named alongside hedgehogs in memo 44994 as banned by Game Commission interpretation.

DC.note: A marsupial, so the 'domesticated rodents and rabbits' category does not reach it.

NYC.quote: All marsupials, including ... numbat and pigmy, sugar and greater glider.

NY.note: Marsupials are not in the definition. NYC bans it separately.

AZ.note: The only marsupial entry is 'All species of the genus Didelphis. Common name: American opossums.'

OR.note: Marsupials are not in the definition.

CA.quote: Domesticated races of golden hamsters of the species Mesocricetus auratus and domesticated races of dwarf hamsters of the Genus Phodopus are not restricted

HI.note: Part A is research and exhibition only, so no pet keeping.

NYC.note: The rodent prohibition reaches only large rodents; hamsters are not named.

CA.note: Order Rodentia is restricted (D) and gerbils are not among the five exceptions, though the order's own heading names them.

GA.note: Rodentia entry excepts Genera Gerbillus and Meriones.

CA.quote: Family Psittacidae-Parrots, Parakeets: Myiopsitta monachus (Monk or Quaker parakeet) (D)

NYC.note: Bird entry covers predatory or large birds only. NY State is a separate question.

NJ.note: Not among the nine exempt birds.

ME.note: Expressly carved out of the unrestricted list: 'Except for: Myiopsitta monachus'.

CA.quote: Domestic cats and hybrids of domestic cats are not restricted

DC.quote: Domestic cats, excluding hybrids with ocelots or margays
DC.note: The Bengal derives from the Asian leopard cat, which is neither.

NYC.quote: All cats other than domesticated cats (Felis catus), including ... any hybrid offspring of a wild cat and domesticated cat.

NY.note: Felidae hybrids are wild animals except registered hybrids with no wild felid ancestry for five or more generations, so an F5 or later Bengal qualifies. NYC bans all wild-cat hybrids regardless.

CA.note: The reptile list covers crocodilians, snapping turtles, venomous snakes and the Gila monster only.

GA.note: Reptile list names two pythons, the Argentine tegu and the Nile monitor only.

DC.note: Lizards are absent from the permitted list entirely.

NYC.note: Chamaeleonidae absent from the reptile entry.

MA.note: Except species categorically nonexempt under endangered species protections.

CO.quote: All non-native tropical and subtropical species of lizards ... Chamaeleonidae (chameleons)

WA.note: Varanidae covers water and crocodile monitors only; no chameleons.

OH.note: The only lizard listed is the Komodo dragon.

GA.note: Testudines list names only Pelomedusa subrufa and Pelodiscus sinensis.

DC.note: Statute says 'turtles'; a tortoise is Testudines, so this is defensible rather than express.

ME.note: Maine's list mislabels it 'Greek Tortoise'. The binomial is Horsfield's/Russian; Greek is T. graeca.

CA.note: Restricted snakes are venomous families plus boomslang, twig snakes and Nerodia.

NYC.quote: any member of the family Pythonidae, including but not limited to the African rock python, Indian or Burmese python, Amethystine or scrub python
NYC.note: 'Any member' catches the ball python though it is not named.

NJ.note: Not exempt, unlike the boa constrictor.

FL.note: Python regius is not on the prohibited list, unlike the large pythons.

NY.note: The reptile entry names venomous species plus Burmese, reticulated and African rock pythons. Python regius is not among them.

MA.quote: All species of boas and pythons (family Boidae)
MA.note: Except African rock python, reticulated python and anacondas.

WA.note: Listed snakes are venomous families plus the boomslang.

OH.note: Restricted constrictors are the anacondas plus reticulated, Indian, Burmese, North and South African rock and amethystine pythons. Python regius is not among them.

NYC.quote: any member, or hybrid offspring of the family Boidae, including ... the common or green anaconda and yellow anaconda

NJ.note: New Jersey exempts the boa and requires a permit for the ball python, the reverse of most states.

MA.quote: All species of boas and pythons (family Boidae)

CO.quote: All non-native tropical and subtropical species of snakes in the families: Boidae (giant snakes)

NYC.quote: All venomous spiders, including, but not limited to, tarantula, black widow and solifugid

GA.note: Reptiles on the list are limited to scientific, educational or public exhibition purposes, but may be held as pets if possessed before the rule's effective date.

NYC.quote: any member of the family Teiidae, including, but not limited to the golden, common, or black and white tegu

FL.quote: genera Salvator and Tupinambis, all species
FL.note: Grandfathered personal permit if possessed before 29 April 2021 and applied for by October 2021, for the life of that animal. Commercial breeding ended 30 June 2024.

NYC.quote: any member of the family Varanidae, including the white throated monitor, Bosc's or African savannah monitor

GA.note: Cynomys is not among the excepted rodent genera.

DC.note: A rodent, but not a domesticated one.

NYC.quote: All large rodents (Rodentia), including ... prairie dog, capybara

MA.note: Absent from the exemption list, so a permit is required.

CO.note: Absent from the unregulated list, so it falls back to licensing. Colorado has native prairie dogs, which is likely why.

AZ.quote: The family Sciuridae. Common names include: chipmunks, marmots, prairie dogs, squirrels, and woodchucks.

NYC.quote: All large rodents (Rodentia), including ... prairie dog, capybara

GA.note: Order Carnivora, all species; only the ferret is excepted.

NYC.quote: All dogs other than domesticated dogs (Canis familiaris), including ... dhole, fennec, raccoon dog

NY.quote: (with the exception of domesticated dogs and captive bred fennec foxes (vulpes zerda))
NY.note: Expressly carved out of the Canidae entry. Legal statewide, banned in NYC.

CT.quote: The canidae, including, but not limited to, the wolf, and coyote

AZ.quote: All species of the order Carnivora

OR.note: Non-wolf, non-indigenous Canidae, with the same closed permit route.

WA.note: The Canidae entry covers wolves only.

OH.note: The canid entries are gray wolves and African wild dogs only.

TX.note: The canids listed are the coyote and jackal only.

NYC.quote: All cats other than domesticated cats (Felis catus), including ... serval, caracal

CT.quote: The felidae, including, but not limited to, the lion, leopard, cheetah, jaguar, ocelot, jaguarundi cat, puma, lynx and bobcat

AZ.quote: All species of the order Carnivora

OR.note: Non-indigenous Felidae. Permits had to pre-date the 2009 Act, so there is no route for a new animal.

WA.note: The Felidae entry names eight big cats and the serval is not among them, so Washington is unusually permissive here.

OH.quote: Servals, excluding hybrids with domestic cats commonly known as savannah cats
OH.note: The serval itself is a dangerous wild animal; savannah cat hybrids are expressly carved out.

TX.quote: a lion; a tiger; an ocelot; a cougar; a leopard; a cheetah; a jaguar; a bobcat; a lynx; a serval; a caracal; a hyena; a bear; a coyote; a jackal; a baboon; a chimpanzee; an orangutan; a gorilla; or any hybrid
TX.note: Certificate of registration plus $100,000 liability insurance.

CA.quote: Domesticated races of chinchillas of the species Chinchilla laniger are not restricted

NJ.note: Not on the exempt list, unlike the hamster and gerbil.

MA.quote: Chinchilla (Chinchilla spp.) derived from captive stock

CA.quote: Domesticated races of guinea pigs of the species Cavia porcellus are not restricted

NYC.quote: any member of the family Iguanidae, including the green or common iguana

FL.note: Same grandfather permit route as the tegu.

NYC.quote: all members of the family Chelydridae, including snapping turtle and alligator snapping turtle

FL.note: Grandfathered for holders of a valid reptile of concern licence.
Grandfathered for personal use by reptile of concern licence holders before 1 July 2010, for the life of the animal.

OH.note: A restricted snake, so it needs a permit rather than being outright banned.
